terms.gloss: look here, you! (in a vehement question or a scolding)
evidence: Plaut. Merc. 1.2.77; Ter. And. 5.4.5 (Lewis & Short s.v. eho)

phrases.latin: Pater, «Heus, dā mihi manum!» identidem clāmitāns
phrases.english: Dad, calling out again and again, “Hey, give me your hand!”

phrases.latin: «Heus tū!» inquit pater, custōdem agēns. «Quis es?»
phrases.english: “Hey, you!” said Dad, playing the guard. “Who are you?”
phrases.source: Libellus V, Lisbōna: castellum et ōceanārium

phrases.latin: sed heus tū! quid agis? ecquid fit?
phrases.english: But hey, you! How are you? Anything happening?
Hey you, I’m talking to you!

sources: Lewis & Short: heus · Lewis & Short: eho

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
Cicero’s letter as in the Latinitas loci collection (loci-cicero-epistulae).
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 328, 341.
